name: Noam Chomsky
role: American linguist and political writer, MIT professor emeritus; anarcho-syndicalist critic of US foreign policy and of corporate power
summary: Chomsky calls himself a libertarian socialist in the anarchist tradition: he wants workplaces and communities run by their participants, regards private corporate power and state bureaucracies as illegitimate authorities, and treats Leninist states as the opposite of socialism. He criticizes US and allied foreign policy as imperial, defends near-absolute free speech, and argues that media and elites manufacture consent. In the short term he defends state social protections and votes tactically.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Calls national health insurance an obviously sensible reform, cheaper and more efficient than the present system, favored by large majorities, and presents single-payer coverage as something the left should defend for people living with problems today.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Notes that the minimum wage tracked productivity until the mid-1960s and that letting it keep doing so would roughly double it, calling that 'nothing radical' and just obvious sense.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Treats talk of a free market as 'something of a joke': actual policy mixes protection, intervention and subsidy for the powerful, and he argues the claim that markets serve people is ideology rather than practice.

public-ownership.rationale: Mixed: he rejects state ownership as leading to 'bureaucratic despotism' and wants workers' and community control instead, yet he also describes public provision such as health insurance and 'public ownership' as part of authentic socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Describes the deep cuts in taxes on the very wealthy and corporations since the 1970s as deliberate decisions that can be reversed, notes strong public support for returning to higher taxes on them, and lists higher taxes on the rich among popular policies blocked by elites.

unions-good.rationale: Presents the crushing of unions as a blow to the labor movement 'and that means to American democracy', benefiting only a small enriched sector; he repeatedly credits organized labor and popular movements with the gains workers won.

property-fundamental.rationale: Says a consistent libertarian socialist opposes private ownership of the means of production, endorsing Proudhon's remark that such property is a form of theft, and treats capitalist property relations as 'fundamentally antihuman'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Says he would defend and even strengthen elements of state authority now, because they are needed to curb the rollback of rights by unaccountable corporate power; elsewhere endorses enforcing health and safety regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Repeatedly condemns welfare cutbacks as a deliberate transfer to the rich and defends social programs (health insurance, Social Security, school lunches) as things the public wants and needs.

worker-ownership.rationale: Argues that industry should be owned and controlled by the workers and the communities, through workers' councils; in 2016 says worker-owned and -managed production should be pursued alongside community budgeting.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Criticises the creation of a surveillance state and argues that privacy should not have to be defended.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Favors decriminalization and calls marijuana decriminalization 'very sensible', treating hard drugs through prevention and treatment, while saying nobody knows the full effects and that experiments are needed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Defends civil liberties for views he finds repugnant, arguing that free expression must be defended most vigorously for horrendous ideas, and criticizes laws and harassment aimed at such speakers.

state-harmful.rationale: Says he shares the anarchist vision of dismantling state power and endorses Humboldt's description of the state as profoundly anti-human, while stressing that for now he defends parts of state authority against private power.

limit-guns.rationale: Calls opposition to gun control 'sadly misguided': guns in citizens' hands will not tame the government, only make the country 'more brutal, ruthless and destructive'.

empower-police-military.rationale: Criticizes the Clinton crime bill's 100,000 more police and heavier punishments as pandering to fear and controlling a 'useless population' by force; condemns US military dominance and arms spending.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: he favors decision-making in workplace and community councils, yet argues for defending the central state against private power for now.

more-religion-public.rationale: Says the impact of fundamentalist religion on social policy has commonly been harmful, if not pernicious, while valuing the community role of religious groups.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Says every civilized country rightly tries to compensate for discrimination and repression, including by giving priority to students from severely disadvantaged groups.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Defends the UN Charter order but says the UN is routinely neutralized by the US, and criticizes the IMF and the World Bank, so no uniform position.

free-trade.rationale: Rejects the idea that free-market doctrines benefit everyone: calls the policies a disaster for the Third World and for most people in rich countries, and says 'free trade' agreements are investor-rights deals masquerading as free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Calls for international solidarity and criticizes elites who pursue narrow national interests; sets US interests behind global cooperation on climate and nuclear risks.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Says one can imagine genuine cases of humanitarian intervention but that the burden of proof is heavy and historical cases are mostly pretexts.

open-borders.rationale: Calls a no-state settlement, with elimination of borders and free transit, the best long-term solution, and wants to reverse the militarization of the Mexico-US border.

limit-growth.rationale: Says growth is not a good thing in itself and may be a bad one, and that reducing consumption-based growth would be healthy for society and future generations, favoring high-speed rail, weatherization and more localism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change, with nuclear war, the greatest threat to organized human life and says urgent, drastic action is required, including at the expense of fossil-fuel interests.

revolution-justified.rationale: Regards violent revolution as a last resort to be avoided where possible, which implies it can sometimes be justified.

experts-over-public.rationale: Attacks the technocratic view, voiced by McNamara-style managers, that decisions belong at the top with experts, as the voice of a technical intelligentsia that distrusts popular control.

central-planning.rationale: Criticises bureaucratic, autocratic control of the economy by the state and by Leninist parties as the opposite of socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Favours producer and community control of production within an economy that remains partly market-based, but does not address markets themselves.

basic-income.rationale: Says a basic income 'could have a place' but is too crude an instrument for the society he wants; his view depends on the wider socioeconomic context.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Says wage slavery should end and labor lose its commodity character; describes a society where work is freely chosen and not compelled by the market, though he treats this as a long-term aim.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rejects the 'red bureaucracy' of vanguard parties as the negation of socialism, warning that revolutionaries given power become worse than the tsar.

democracy-best.rationale: Treats real democracy as an unfulfilled ideal and rejects the claim that people are unready for freedom, citing Rousseau and Kant that they learn it only by exercising it.

direct-votes.rationale: Favours direct participation in decisions rather than representative government alone, through councils and general assemblies.

workers-councils.rationale: Argues that council communism is the natural form of revolutionary socialism in an industrial society, with councils of workers replacing a state and its political parties.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rejects the claim that some people are unfit for freedom, quoting Kant's refusal to accept that some are not ready, and Rousseau on the 'happy slave' apologists.

political-violence-never.rationale: Treats nonviolence as a tactic whose merits depend on conditions, not an absolute principle, and says everyone is for nonviolence in the abstract.

military-superiority.rationale: Condemns Washington's drive to extend its 'historically unique military dominance' as accelerating the race to destruction, and objects to adding US forces off China's coast.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Says market systems turn people into sociopaths who look out only for themselves, and contrasts the libertarian-socialist ideal with competitive greed and predatory individualism.

direct-action.rationale: Says elections matter but are 'not the main issue', that the main work is sustained popular organizing and pressure; he still advises voting in swing states.

means-match-ends.rationale: Quotes with approval Buber's line that a little tree turned into a club cannot put forth leaves, and Luxemburg on the creative role of mass participation, arguing that authoritarian means undermine libertarian ends.

distribute-by-need.rationale: States that the society to aim for would respect the principle 'to each according to their needs', and goes on to describe the needs that principle should meet.

production-for-use.rationale: Observes that under capitalism the economy is steered by power, growth and profit and not by human needs, and argues that decisions made collectively would better express those needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Sets out, approvingly, the classical-liberal and Marxist critique of wage labor as a bondage worse than slavery and a theory of exploitation, and calls capitalist relations of production antihuman.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Condemns Leninist dictatorial rule over workers in the name of the proletariat and favors direct workers' power over structures run by a party leadership.

taxation-theft.rationale: Dismisses the reflex that taxes are bureaucrats 'stealing our money' as the product of business propaganda; says Americans are undertaxed by comparative standards and endorses pooled public provision.

harm-principle.rationale: Says secular values include respect for individual choice 'as long as it does not harm others', and that state power should not intrude on personal matters like dress.

positive-liberty.rationale: Treats freedom as needing material conditions and social protection, holding that unconstrained markets destroy the conditions of existence and need state corrective action.

media-academia-power.rationale: Says conservative claims that the university faculty is mostly Marxist are wrong; the faculty are moderate liberals, and he locates real power in private corporate power more than in media or academia.

total-state.rationale: Holds that the state is a profoundly anti-human institution and that state socialism leads to bureaucratic despotism, opposing any state direction of all life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Describes US continental expansion as settler-colonial conquest, the cruelest form of imperialism, and criticizes the celebration of conquest.

universal-morality.rationale: Calls the principle of universality, applying to oneself the standards applied to others, among the most elementary moral truisms; does not discuss reason or cross-cultural moral truth generally.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Contested: he says he has opposed a Jewish state since the 1930s, as he would a Muslim, white or Christian state, while also accepting that both national groups in Palestine have a right to self-determination.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Says democracy is a sham while the industrial system is run by an autocratic elite and that reforms cannot bring freedom without democratic control of the workplace; calls this the central issue for the left.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backs self-determination for Palestinians and East Timorese yet calls the nation-state system brutal and prefers a no-state or binational settlement.

force-without-un.rationale: Says the UN Charter bans the threat or use of force unless the Security Council authorizes it or in self-defense, and calls US action outside that framework illegal.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Says irrational belief is dangerous and he avoids it personally, but defends respect for others' beliefs and notes efforts against false beliefs must be tailored, not a call for reason alone.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposes apartheid and the legal segregation of races, calling Israel's treatment of Palestinians worse than South Africa's.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Condemns the expansion of fossil fuel production, including coal, and says opposing Trump's fossil-fuel policies is part of why voters should pick the Democrat in swing states.

national-mission.rationale: Treats the American claim of a moral mission as self-flattering propaganda, calling reflections on America's 'tragic flaw' of idealism an embarrassment.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Says he certainly uses the concept of patriarchy, counts domination of women in the home among the illegitimate authorities anarchism challenges, and notes that half the population's work goes uncounted.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cites with approval that most Americans see the political system as serving special interests and says the political parties are largely run by corporate and wealthy interests, though he mostly describes capture rather than corruption.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejects the American libertarian program of minimal government as a cover for unaccountable corporate tyranny, and defends state action (regulation, health insurance, social protection).

socialism-one-country.rationale: Endorses the Leninist point that socialism needs joint effort of workers in several advanced countries and uses it to argue that a revolutionary movement in the US is essential.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Says Zionism has been a settler-colonial movement and that the concept applies to the pre-1948 period, and describes the US as a settler-colonial state that exterminated its indigenous population.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Objects to school prayer pushed by Gingrich as state coercion of six-year-olds who cannot freely walk out; speaks about prayer, not religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Doubts that more dictatorial structures would have better defended the Spanish revolution and suggests a more consistent libertarian policy might have been the only possible defense.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Names competitiveness among the features of capitalist relations that are antihuman, preferring free association and social bonds.

vanguard-party.rationale: Says the vanguard party is a 'soulful' autocracy and that those urging submission to benevolent autocracies wish to turn people into machines; sides with council communism.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes state or party censorship and control of media, and contrasts it unfavorably with even the subtler corporate system; defends free expression against state suppression.

recall-officials.rationale: Favours revocable representatives in principle, but the recall of elected officials is not separately addressed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Criticises NATO expansion as a provocation and opposes a stronger NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Says the death penalty is a crime and that the state should have no right to take lives, agreeing with Amnesty International.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Argues that much Third World debt is 'odious' under the very principle the US used for Cuba, which would wipe out a large share of it, and says Nicaragua's debt could be erased by the World Court's reparations judgment alone.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports the international consensus of Israeli withdrawal from the occupied territories and faults the US and Israel for blocking it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Argues the Soviet system destroyed socialism by crushing workers' control, calls Leninist regimes 'state capitalist' managers' societies, and says their collapse was a small victory for socialism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Says Israel's settlement of the territories conquered in 1967 is illegal settlement under military occupation, and notes the annexation of East Jerusalem was in defiance of the UN.

refugee-return.rationale: Describes the Palestinian refugees' right of return, endorsed by the UN General Assembly, as being erased in the Oslo settlement, in terms that show he regards it as a right; he does not address descendants.

no-bailouts.rationale: Criticizes bank and investor bailouts, such as for Mexico's creditors, as state protection of the rich that contradicts market principles; does not state a general rule.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Defends affirmative-action style priority for disadvantaged groups in admissions and criticizes the US for doing too little of it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: His propaganda model says the media inculcate the values and codes of behavior that integrate people into existing institutional structures, serving the interests of the dominant elite.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Argues that in societies with formal freedom the powerful manage opinion through propaganda and by fixing the premises of discourse, the 'manufacture of consent' described by Lippmann.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Describes a system of workers' and consumers' councils and federations where representation is 'direct and revocable', delegates remaining answerable to the groups that send them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Opposes privatizing Social Security: says the fund can be invested either way and that individual accounts break down solidarity and the sense of responsibility for one another.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Says growth driven by consumption is not good in itself and that market systems turn people into self-regarding sociopaths; maximizing commodities is not the measure of a decent life.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Condemns US arming of the Nicaraguan contras as terrorism and cites the World Court's ruling against it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Treats Soviet imperialism as real for the Hungarians and Czechs and condemns superpower domination of client states on both sides.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says private power exerts an inordinately heavy influence on the political system through control of the media, political organizations and by supplying its top personnel; his propaganda-model work and later interviews return to this constantly.

democratic-peace.rationale: Says the European 'democratic peace' is traceable to the lessons of centuries of nation-state wars, and that it is far from clear that democracy has much to do with it.

non-intervention.rationale: Does not hold an absolute ban: grants that genuine humanitarian intervention is conceivable but demands very strong justification.

defeat-communism.rationale: Argues the Cold War crusade served domestic control and economic aims, and that Soviet 'communism' is not socialism; favors diplomatic accommodation.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Opposes semi-privatized, privately run but publicly funded school systems as unproven and corrosive of solidarity; this concerns schools only.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Calls the Israeli kibbutzim the most dramatic example of long-lived anarchist-style self-management; his broader model is federations of workplace and neighborhood communities.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Said the claim that there were no gas chambers is 'highly implausible' and that denial of the Holocaust is completely so, while defending the civil rights of those who deny it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemns repression of dissent by states of every kind, including Leninist states, and defends freedom of expression for opponents.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Argues for direct popular control over all institutions, by those who take part in and are affected by them, in workplaces as well as communities.

alienated-labor.rationale: Develops the account of alienated labor, work external to the worker, from Humboldt and the early Marx, and says industrial capitalism's wage slavery is in fundamental opposition to human creativity.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Says there should be no laws forcing women to remove veils or other preferred dress, and that what people wear is not the state's business, asked about the French law on religious symbols.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Calls IMF-style austerity programs disastrous for populations and says Argentina was right not to pay 'odious' creditors; does not explicitly state that governments should refuse the conditions.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: His propaganda model holds that concentrated ownership, advertising and wealth let money and power filter the news and marginalize dissent, so that the media serve dominant elites.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argues that extreme concentrations of wealth translate into political power and weaken democracy, favors the Aristotelian solution of reducing inequality over Madison's solution of limiting democracy.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Treats nuclear war and climate catastrophe as the gravest threats to human survival that require priority action by all governments.

abolish-ip.rationale: Says copyright is neither the moral nor the efficient way to support creative work and that society should fund the arts democratically so artists would not need it; calls the WTO patent regime protectionist and harmful.

independent-unions.rationale: Condemns the 'Stalinist-style' government-run union in Suharto's Indonesia and the brutal suppression of attempts to create independent unions there.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Insists that real socialism means workers' direct control over production through councils, and that a vanguard or state bureaucracy ruling in their name is its negation.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Envisages workers' councils, commune assemblies and regional federations in which delegates come from, and return to, their own organic communities.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Sets out the UN Charter rule that force is allowed only in self-defense against armed attack until the Security Council acts, and treats breaches as crimes.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Said a carbon tax is basically a good idea and that urgent measures are needed; does not say taxes should replace regulation.

future-generations.rationale: Warns that climate destruction may leave a planet that cannot sustain organized human life 'in anything like a form we would want to tolerate', a danger that falls on coming generations.

arms-reduction.rationale: Agrees with those calling for abolishing nuclear weapons, calls current nuclear programs and war plans an abomination, and warns about weaponization of space.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Calls for finishing with the state in a revolution, though his position on the form of the transition is not spelled out.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Mocks 'right-to-work' laws as 'right-to-scrounge' laws: they give the right to be represented by a union without paying for it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Says democracy is largely a sham where the industrial system is controlled by an autocratic elite, and criticizes representative democracy for being limited to the political sphere.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Says that if the Nuremberg standards were applied, every postwar US president would have been hanged, and that US refusal of International Criminal Court jurisdiction defies majority American opinion.

indirect-election.rationale: Defends a council system where higher bodies are staffed by delegates from lower ones, who keep taking part in their own work and rotate, as a barrier to remote bureaucracy.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Calls means testing of benefits 'cumbersome and degrading' and contrasts it with the universal provision standard in the civilized world.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Describes James Tobin's proposed tax on currency speculation as plausibly able to shift capital to productive uses and finds the explanation for elite opposition to it persuasive.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Says that insofar as robots and automation free people from routine and dangerous work for creative activity and leisure, 'that's all to the good'.

material-over-identity.rationale: Says Democrats focus on identity politics, which is 'okay' but not class-based and does not appeal to most people's needs, and urges rebuilding labor-based movements.

notes:
Based mostly on his own texts: full-text books (Manufacturing Consent, Profit Over People, How the World Works, Keeping the Rabble in Line, Class Warfare, Necessary Illusions, Fateful Triangle, Failed States, Rogue States, Chomsky on Anarchism) and chomsky.info articles and interviews. Understanding Power, Hegemony or Survival, Requiem for the American Dream and Who Rules the World? (English) could not be read in full text (Internet Archive lending copies or only a non-English edition), so nothing rests on them. Recent position wins where views changed: he calls a two-state settlement the best practical path but prefers binational or no-state arrangements, and he accepts strategic voting for Democrats in swing states since 2016. Wikipedia pages are used only as secondary pointers and for the Nuremberg remark and copyright quotation.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 9 answers taken from it, 43 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Positions are drawn from his own articles and interviews on chomsky.info plus Wikipedia as a reference. Coverage is strongest on economy, government, world affairs and the media. Israel-Palestine: his stated preference shifted over decades (a binational or one-state option in the 1970s-2000s, a two-state international-consensus settlement by 2023), so the 2023 interview is taken as the most recent clear view. Faurisson: he defended the right of expression, and his 1980 essay does not endorse Faurisson's claims. Wikipedia reports a 2023 stroke with loss of ability to speak or walk, so no newer positions are recorded. Books (Understanding Power, Requiem for the American Dream, Who Rules the World?, Hegemony or Survival) were not downloaded separately; the chomsky.info texts used include the book-related talks and interviews. 'Government in the Future' (1970) was not found in the chomsky.info index. Most statements are null because the corpus does not address them.
